item.title: District attorney candidates discuss priorities for Buncombe County
item.description: Courtney Booth, Katie Kurdys and Martin Moore are the three Democratic candidates running for Buncombe County District Attorney in this year's March 3 primary. No Republican is running.

item.title: Two deaths, failure to isolate infectious diseases led to Mission’s latest Immediate Jeopardy
item.description: The issues cited by state investigators are familiar to those who have followed Mission’s struggles since its acquisition by HCA: inadequate staffing, poor controls and insufficient steps to address past mistakes.

item.title: Asheville Poetry Review’s founder reflects on journal’s finale and his difficult new chapter
item.description: After three decades, the celebrated journal enters its denouement as founder Keith Flynn grapples with illness.

item.title: Town of Canton is the latest to consider banning crypto mining, data centers
item.description: The Town of Canton is considering banning cryptocurrency mining and data centers after repeated inquiries about using its former paper mill site, with town leaders citing harmful impacts seen in other rural communities and concerns that environmental and infrastructure costs would outweigh potential tax revenue.

item.title: The Playlist: Silas Durocher of The Get Right Band offers psychedelic selections to calm our nerves
item.description: "I find myself listening to a lot of music like what's on this playlist — songs that are laid-back and calming and spacious enough to leave room for my mind to wander — because it feels healthy for my nervous system," says Silas Durocher.

item.title: How do reparations address health disparities?
item.description: Last October, the Community Reparations Commission wrapped up their final 39 recommendations on how to invest nearly $4 million in reparations funds. Here's a deep dive into the Health & Wellness recommendations.

item.title: Commission hears updates on winter storms, Code Purple
item.description: “We are seeing a huge level of need this year — I think more than any of us were anticipating,” Lacy Hoyle, the Community Development Homelessness Program manager, told the Buncombe County Board of Commissioners.

item.title: Pro tip: Movement is medicine
item.description: "I love music, and when I get a song that I can’t get enough of, I love starting my day dancing as wildly and goofy as my body wants to," Heather Parmley, a massage therapist, yoga teacher and retreat facilitator through her business Awaken Wellness Retreats.

item.title: Buncombe Commissioner Horton sues the county
item.description: Horton filed the suit Feb. 2 in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of North Carolina. It alleges that, after she was elected to the board, the county illegally suspended funding for five adult care homes she had been operating through her business, Living Waters Enterprises.

item.title: Tips and reminders about the blood-donating process
item.description: There are two predominant organizations in Western North Carolina where people can donate blood. The Western North Carolina Chapter of the America Red Cross and The Blood Connection both have brick-and-mortar locations, plus a fleet of bloodmobiles which roam the region to host blood drives.
